description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Initial Accuracy, Final Accuracy, and Δ Accuracy—on the MMLU benchmark, as described in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans a linear range from 0.86 to 1.00, with tick marks at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” is linear and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with major gridlines every 0.2 units. The “Final Accuracy” (blue solid line with circle markers) remains consistently high across all confidence levels, hovering near 0.95–1.00, with minor fluctuations and error bars indicating low variance. The “Initial Accuracy” (green dashed line with square markers) starts at approximately 0.65 at 0.86 confidence, rises steadily to a peak of ~0.92 at 0.97 confidence, then declines to ~0.77 at 1.00 confidence. The “Δ Accuracy” (orange dash-dotted line with diamond markers), representing the improvement from initial to final accuracy, begins at ~0.28 at 0.86 confidence, drops to a low of ~0.05 around 0.95 confidence, and rises again to ~0.22 at 1.00 confidence, indicating that the model’s ability to improve via feedback is not uniform across confidence levels.
